title: Audio of Surrey RCMP shooting of Hudson Brooks posted online
subtitle: Police audio of the last moments of Hudson Brooks\'s life broke his mother Jennifer\'s heart all over again.
article: Police audio of the last moments of Hudson Brooks\'s life broke his mother Jennifer\'s heart all over again.

Hudson Brooks died in a police-involved shooting near an RCMP community policing detachment in the 1800-block of 152nd Street in south Surrey on July 18, 2015 after officers responded to a call about a suicidal man in distress.

An audio clip which appears to record the exchange between police officers and dispatch was posted last Friday on YouTube by a user who regularly uploads audio of police-related incidents gathered through radio traffic and scanner recordings.
Jennifer Brooks said she got a call from the Independent Investigations Office on Tuesday, informing her of the tape\'s presence online. She left work to listen to it at home.

"It was devastating," said Brooks on Thursday, which would have been Hudson\'s 22nd birthday. "It was so heartbreaking. There was no \'stop, put up your hands,\' nothing. Within seconds of them calling upon him, he was shot. He didn\'t stand a chance."
There was nothing in the audio tape she didn\'t know, but listening to how the fatal incident unfolded still left her shaken. "How this went so wrong so quickly is unfathomable," said Brooks.
In the recording, a female voice could be heard describing Hudson, who was not wearing a shirt or shoes, "yelling \'kill me, kill me, kill me\'."
At 52 seconds into the tape, a male voice was heard saying: "I got something right here coming directly at me." Seconds later: "I need help now. I need help now," then a report of "shots fired."
Later, a female voice was heard saying, "I shot myself," followed by a male calling for emergency services. "Suspect is critical. We need a code. We need it now."
The audio lasts 2 minutes and 41 seconds.

The IIO said it was aware of the tape and had requested it be removed "as this is an open investigation which has been referred to Crown counsel," said spokesman Aidan Buckley. The source of the information does not appear linked to the IIO, he said.

Brooks said she doesn\'t want to listen to the tape again, but does not object to it being in the public domain, unless it jeopardizes the investigation. "Otherwise, the public needs to hear what happened," said Brooks, who wants answers and more de-escalation training for officers
The IIO completed its report into Brooks\' death in October, and forwarded a file to Crown "for consideration of charges."
The police watchdog agency does not make recommendations on whether charges should be approved. The threshold for referral to Crown is lower for the IIO than for police agencies.
